title: Seat a flanged bushing with a manual arbor press
instruction: Press the bushing until its flange sits flat against the housing, then raise the ram and let go of the handle.
context: A machine assembler or repair technician seats a replaceable plain bearing in a pivot housing. A visible flange checks that the bushing reached its stop.
setup: A compact cast-iron press is bolted to the bench at (420, -125) mm relative to the arms. Its steel hand lever has a 160 mm grip radius and its flat platen is 34.6 mm wide. The 52 by 52 by 39 mm steel housing on the anvil is centered at (402, -125) mm. The 35 mm flange OD polymer bushing starts square in the housing chamfer, with its flange 15 mm above the housing. The ram is raised and hands are clear.
scoring: After unloading and moving the hands clear, score 0.5 for at least 7.5 mm retained axial advance produced by the press. Score 1.0 for a square, intact flange seated all around with no gap over 0.20 mm and stable for 1 s. Use video, a feeler gauge and height datum. Score 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Raise the ram. Start a fresh reference bushing square at the housing chamfer and verify the 15 mm flange gap.
fidelity: A native rack-and-pinion joint couples the contact-driven lever and ram. Rigid sleeve and steel housing colliders preserve the flange stop. A coaxial guide and 35 N force-limited yielding drive approximate the already-started interference fit. The value is provisional and does not establish real polymer deformation or insertion force.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 (264 actions, 39.04 s wall time). Dream-1 beta 0.0 (1,200 actions, 125.80 s wall time). Both trials used seed 17 and the same native camera and physics configuration.
